validity.researcher_notes: This row is real, correctly classified, and not a duplicate. It is Columbia Gas Transmission's (TC Energy subsidiary) Eastern Panhandle Expansion Project, FERC Docket CP17-80-000: an 8-inch, 3.37-3.4 mi interstate lateral built from Columbia's existing Line 1804/1024 0 interconnects in Fulton County, PA, through Washington County, MD, to a point of delivery with the LDC Mountaineer Gas Company in Morgan County, WV. Confirmed independently by (1) FERC's own Federal Register Notice of Application (82 FR 16390, filed by Columbia Gas Transmission LLC on 2017-03-15), (2) TC Energy's own project factsheet, (3) EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook (every release 2018-08 through 2026-08, docket CP17-80, operator 'Columbia Gas Transmission'), and (4) independent trade press (Pipeline & Gas Journal, July and November 2025) reporting the project was placed in service June 26, 2025. No roster row duplicates this segment - Mountaineer Gas Pipeline appears only once (P2009) in the 42-row roster. Classification as a gas transmission lateral is correct (FERC Natural Gas Act section 7(c) interstate certificate; delivers to an LDC, consistent with GEM's 'transmission' PipelineType convention). Owner/Operator = Columbia Gas Transmission LLC, 100%, confirmed by name in the FERC docket, EIA's operator field, and TC Energy's site. Minor unverified detail: the sheet's EndLocation 'Berkeley Springs' (the Morgan County seat) was not found stated verbatim in any source - sources confirm the point of delivery is in Morgan County, WV generally, not that the literal interconnection is at the town of Berkeley Springs. Not material enough to contest given the county-level location is solidly sourced.

validity.recommendation: Correct Capacity from 4750.00 MMcf/d to approximately 47 MMcf/d - almost certainly a decimal-point/order-of-magnitude data entry error (e.g. '47.50' typed as '4750'). An 8-inch, 3.4-mile lateral cannot physically carry 4,750 MMcf/d (Baird's sanity flag is correct). FERC's 2017 application (Docket CP17-80) authorized 47,500 Dth/d (~47.5 MMcf/d) of firm transportation; TC Energy's own factsheet states 'more than 47 million cubic feet per day'; EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook records 47.5 MMcf/d Additional Capacity through 2025-07 and 47.0 MMcf/d from 2026-01 onward; and Pipeline & Gas Journal's July 2025 in-service article states 'delivering 47 million cubic feet per day'. Four independent origins (FERC/Federal Register, the operator TC Energy, EIA, and trade press) converge on ~47 MMcf/d.
validity.researcher_notes: See recommendation. Sources: FERC Federal Register Notice of Application (82 FR 16390, 2017-03-15 filing date) states '47,500 Dekatherms per day (Dth/d) of firm transportation service' - 1 Dth is approximately 1 Mcf, so this is ~47.5 MMcf/d. TC Energy's factsheet: 'more than 47 million cubic feet per day'. EIA workbook (all 28 releases 2018-05 through 2026-08, docket CP17-80): additional_capacity_mmcf_d = 47.5 (releases through 2025-07) then 47.0 (releases 2026-01 onward, i.e. post-completion reporting) - cite the Aug 2026 release, sheet 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)', Excel row 1191, https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/pipelines/EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjectsAug2026.xlsx. Pipeline & Gas Journal, July 2025: 'delivering 47 million cubic feet per day'. The routes-repo geojson (../GOIT-GGIT-pipeline-routes/data/individual-routes/gas-pipelines/P2009.geojson, digitized from the FERC Environmental Assessment) independently carries 'Additional': 46.6, 'ProductUni': 'MMscf/d' as internal corroboration, though that file is not itself a citable web reference. The sheet's 4750.00 MMcf/d is off by roughly 100x from every source found.
